tower-of-hanoi.title: Place largest disk on target first
tower-of-hanoi.principle: If the largest disk is not already on the goal peg, move it directly to the goal peg before moving any smaller disks onto that peg. This guarantees the largest disk ends up at the bottom and prevents illegal placements.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: When the initial configuration has the largest disk on a different peg than the goal peg and the goal peg is empty (or contains only larger disks, which cannot happen).
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving smaller disks onto the goal peg before moving the largest disk there, which later blocks placing the largest disk at the bottom.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Recursive Hanoi move sequence
tower-of-hanoi.principle: To move n disks from a source peg to a target peg using an auxiliary peg, first recursively move n‑1 disks from source to auxiliary, then move the nth (largest) disk from source to target, and finally recursively move the n‑1 disks from auxiliary to target.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: Whenever a stack of disks must be transferred between pegs while respecting the size rule.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Attempting to move the whole stack in one step without breaking it into sub‑problems, resulting in illegal or incomplete moves.

tower-of-hanoi.title: Validate each move's legality
tower-of-hanoi.principle: Before committing a move, ensure the disk being moved is the topmost on its source peg and that the destination peg's top disk (if any) is larger than the moving disk.
tower-of-hanoi.when_to_apply: During construction of the move list, after each planned move.
tower-of-hanoi.example: Moving a larger disk onto a smaller one, which violates the Tower of Hanoi rule.

tower-of-hanoi.why_it_happens: The model may stop reasoning before generating moves or forget to translate its plan into the required output format.
tower-of-hanoi.how_to_avoid: Always construct and output a non‑empty move list that transforms the initial configuration to the goal, even if the solution is trivial.
